questions.heading: A Vertex Is a Basis: Set n Variables to Zero and Solve for the Rest
questions.stem: An LP has 4 variables and 3 rows of the form a.x <= b. After one slack is added per row, how many of the variables are zero at a basic solution?

options.text: 3, since each of the 3 rows forces one variable to zero
options.says: The 3 rows give 3 equations, which are solved for 3 basic variables; the zeros are the others.

options.text: 7, since a vertex sets the slacks and originals to zero
options.says: Only the nonbasic variables are zero; the basic ones take the values the equations give.

options.text: 4, since 3 of the 7 are solved from the 3 equations
options.says: Right: n = 4 nonbasic variables are set to zero and the m = 3 basic ones are solved for.

options.text: 0, since the equations fix a value for each variable
options.says: Three equations cannot fix seven unknowns; four must be chosen, and they are set to zero.

questions.heading: The Ratio Test Picks the Row That Leaves: the First Basic Variable to Reach Zero
questions.stem: The entering column has entries 2, -1 and 4 in constraint rows 1, 2 and 3, whose right-hand sides are 6, 3 and 20. Which row's basic variable leaves?

options.text: Row 1, since 6 / 2 = 3 is the smallest ratio over positive entries
options.says: Right: row 2's entry is negative and sets no limit; of 6/2 = 3 and 20/4 = 5, row 1 hits zero first.

options.text: Row 2, since 3 / -1 = -3 is the smallest ratio over all entries
options.says: A row with a negative entry gets larger as the variable rises, so it is left out of the test.

options.text: Row 3, since its entry 4 is the largest one in the entering column
options.says: The test compares right-hand side divided by entry, not the entries alone.

options.text: Row 2, since its right-hand side 3 is the smallest of the three rows
options.says: A small right-hand side matters only through its ratio, and row 2's entry is not positive.

questions.heading: When No Objective-Row Entry Is Negative, the Vertex Is Optimal
questions.stem: A maximization tableau's objective row has entries 3, 0.5 and -2 under the nonbasic variables s1, s2 and x3, and 50 on the right. What is the next step?

options.text: Stop at value 50, since most of the objective-row entries are positive
options.says: One negative entry is enough to improve: the test is that no entry is negative.

options.text: Stop at value 50, since s1's entry 3 is the largest in the row
options.says: The size of a positive entry says what raising that variable would cost, not that the vertex is best.

options.text: Enter s1, since its entry 3 is the largest in the objective row
options.says: A positive entry means raising s1 lowers z by 3 per unit; entering variables have negative entries.

options.text: Enter x3, since its entry -2 means raising it adds 2 per unit
options.says: Right: the row says z = 50 - 3 s1 - 0.5 s2 + 2 x3, so x3 improves the objective.
